column1: # Executables the rules invoke, per environment. Checked by .github/workflows/conda-envs.yml.
# Two tab-separated fields: the environment file, then a shell command run inside it.
# `command -v` is the default form, and it is enough for the failure this exists to catch: it fails
# both when a name is absent from bin/ and when it is present as a symlink to a file that does not
# exist, which are the two shapes the bioconda transdecoder package produced in issue #237.
# Real invocations are used only where they assert something `command -v` cannot - that an
# interpreter can import what a script needs, or that an env holds an SDK rather than just a
# runtime. Most bioinformatics tools here have no flag that reliably exits 0, and a guess at one
# reddens the job without anything being wrong, so they are left as `command -v`.
# Coreutils (cp, mv, mkdir, rm, ln, touch, ls, grep, sort, head) are deliberately absent: no
# environment declares them, they come from the host, and checking them would only ever pass.
# test_smoke_commands.py checks this file against the rules, so an environment a rule depends on
# cannot end up here with nothing listed.
